8 curated presets plus a full color picker and hex-code input.
Text, vector graphics, and images all stay on top of the color.

pdf-background-color.formula:
final_pixel = background × opacity + page × (1 − opacity)

where background = your chosen RGB color. At 100% opacity the page behind is fully covered; at 20% you get a gentle tint. The rectangle is drawn first in the page graphics stream, so all original content renders on top of it.
pdf-background-color.workedExample: A 200-page ebook with harsh white pages: choose #fef3c7 (warm paper) at 100% opacity. Every page gets a warm paper background while the text stays exactly as printed — easier on the eyes for long reading sessions, in one download.
benefits: Reading tints reduce eye strain on long documents.
Brand-colored pages for proposals, menus, and certificates.

Hex input for precise brand colors.
No upload; your documents stay on your device.
limitations: Pages that are full-bleed photos or scans won't show the color — the image covers it.
Existing colored backgrounds are covered, not blended, at 100% opacity.
Very dark backgrounds can make dark text hard to read — preview first.
Some printers charge more for full-page color; consider this before printing.

faqs.q: How does the background color work?
faqs.a: The tool draws a full-page colored rectangle behind your page content, then places your original page on top. Text and images are untouched — they just sit on a colored sheet now.

faqs.q: Why can I not see the color on some pages?
faqs.a: If a page is a full-page photo or scan, that image covers the color completely. The background shows wherever the page itself is blank or transparent.

faqs.q: What is a good opacity for reading?
faqs.a: For reading tints, 100% opacity with a light color (like warm paper #fef3c7) works best. Lower opacities are for subtle effects over existing designs.

faqs.q: Can I use my brand exact color?
faqs.a: Yes — type the hex code (e.g. #1e3a8a) into the color field for a precise match.
Yes, the color is part of the PDF. Note that PDF viewers have a 'print backgrounds' setting, and full-page color uses more ink.

faqs.q: Does it work in dark mode?
faqs.a: The preview adapts to your theme. For a dark-reading effect, pick a dark color like #1e293b — light text stays readable on top.
